profile_md:
## Italmatch Chemicals (Dequest / BWA / Compass): investor profile

**Bottom line:** Italmatch is a ~$740m-revenue, ~$145m-EBITDA global specialty-additives manufacturer. It is one of the world's largest phosphonate producers and the owner of the Dequest and BWA water-additive brands. It is **not** a water-treatment service company: it sells active ingredients (phosphonates, polymers, biocides, antiscalants) mostly to the formulators and service companies that are the core of our universe. Roughly **28% of group revenue is true water treatment**. Another ~15% is oilfield production chemicals, ~5% is detergent/other phosphonate uses, and about half is lubricant additives, flame retardants and personal-care ingredients. We estimate US water-treatment revenue at about **$60m**.

### Business overview
The group reports four business units:
- **Advanced Water Solutions (AWS):** 48% of 9M2023 revenue (EUR249.5m of EUR519.0m).
- **Lubricant Performance Additives (LPA):** 30%.
- **Flame Retardants & Plastic Additives (FPA):** 11%.
- **Performance Products & Personal Care (PPA):** 11%.

AWS sells scale and corrosion inhibitors, dispersants, RO/desalination antiscalants and biocides for cooling, boiler, membrane and process water. Its customers are global water-treatment formulators, thermal and membrane desalination plants and detergent makers. AWS also supplies scale, hydrate and corrosion inhibitors to oil & gas producers. Oilfield work is a large part of AWS, especially in North America (Water Science Technologies) and the North Sea (Aubin).

### History and ownership
- **1997:** Founded in Genoa.
- **Pre-2014:** Owned by Mandarin Capital Partners and the Malacalza family.
- **2014-2018:** Ardian (entry EV ~EUR220m).
- **2018:** Bain Capital Private Equity took control at an EV of ~EUR700m, about 10x expected 2018 EBITDA of ~EUR70m (BeBeez).
- **Dec 2022:** Saudi Arabia's Dussur bought a stake below 20%, alongside a EUR100m capital increase. At that time the group had ~1,100 employees, 19 plants and LTM revenue of ~EUR858m.
- **Financing:** EUR800m of senior secured notes due 2028 (fixed and floating; S&P/Moody's single-B area, B3/B cited by CreditSights).
- **Jan 2025:** Bloomberg reported that Bain was exploring a sale at ~EUR1.5bn EV, on LTM sales of EUR695m, adjusted EBITDA of EUR140m and net debt of EUR582m.
- **Sept-Oct 2025:** India's **Dorf Ketal** was reported in exclusive talks to buy Italmatch for ~**$1.6bn**, with CEO Sergio Iorio rolling over. S&P placed the ratings on CreditWatch Positive. **We could not confirm signing or closing.** This is the single most important open question for the ultimate-parent field.

### Products and chemistries
It is vertically integrated in phosphorus chemistry:
- **Phosphonates** (HEDP, ATMP, DTPMP, PBTC) under the ex-Monsanto **Dequest** brand, bought out of the Thermphos bankruptcy in 2013 (~EUR80m of business, plants in the UK, Belgium and Germany).
- **Maleic/acrylic and phosphinocarboxylic polymers and THPS-type biocides** from **BWA Water Additives** (acquired 2019: Belclene, Flocon, Bellacide).
- **Water-soluble polymers** from GRS (Italy, 2014).
- **Selective metal-recovery resins** from Magpie Polymers (France, 2017).

Non-water lines include lubricant additives (Elco/Detrex in Cleveland and Ashtabula OH, 2016; Polartech metalworking additives in Bedford Park IL, 2018), phosphorus-based halogen-free flame retardants, and personal-care ingredients. Almost everything is made in-house; oilfield packages are blended in the US.

### End markets
Total-platform estimate:
- Oil & gas/refining: ~19%
- Other, mostly automotive and industrial lubricants: ~20%
- Manufacturing, including metalworking and E&E plastics: ~15%
- Consumer, including personal care and detergents: ~14%
- Chemicals/plastics compounding: ~9%
- Water-treatment verticals: ~28% in total, spread across power, HVAC, mining, pulp & paper, food & beverage, municipal and others.

There is no pool or agriculture exposure. Water demand is indirect: Italmatch's customers are the Ecolab/Veolia/Kurita/ChemTreat/regional-formulator tier and desalination EPCs. That makes it a **supplier to our universe more than a competitor**, and US water revenue here overlaps with formulator revenue counted elsewhere.

### US footprint
There are nine US locations:
- **Atlanta GA:** sales office and US lead office (the earlier Tucker GA address belonged to legacy BWA/Italmatch USA).
- **Mableton GA:** phosphonate plant and lab (ex-Compass Chemical).
- **Birmingham AL:** blending plant and lab (ex-WST).
- **Cleveland OH and Ashtabula OH:** lubricant additives and other (ex-Elco/Detrex).
- **Bedford Park IL:** metalworking additives (ex-Polartech).
- **Jane Lew WV:** blending/warehouse.
- **Midland TX and Miles City MT:** oilfield warehouses.

Only Mableton, part of Birmingham, and the Atlanta office are water-treatment assets. The WV/TX/MT sites are oilfield logistics.

### Financials
- **FY2024 (reported):** revenue EUR686m (~$742m at 1.082), adjusted EBITDA EUR134m (~$145m, 19.5% margin), up from EUR115m in 2023.
- **Earlier years:** revenue peaked at ~EUR858m LTM in 2022 on inflation pass-through. EBITDA fell in 2023 on destocking (9M margin 15.8% vs 18.8%) and has since recovered.
- **Valuation:** the EUR1.5bn to $1.6bn price talk implies ~10-11x EBITDA.
- **Water share:** applying the 9M2023 unit mix to 2024 gives AWS ~$357m, of which ~$207m is water treatment, ~$110m oilfield and ~$40m detergent/other (all estimates).
- **US water treatment (estimate):** US revenue ~30% (~$220m), of which AWS is ~$140m. Less ~$70m oilfield and ~$10m other leaves **~$60m** (range $45-80m).
- **FY2025 results** were not retrievable (the company site blocked fetches).

### M&A strategy
A serial acquirer built around phosphorus chemistry:
- Water: Dequest 2013, GRS 2014, Solvay phosphorus activity 2016, **Compass Chemical** 2016, Sudamfos 2016, Magpie 2017, Jiayou phosphonates 2018, **BWA** 2019.
- Oilfield: **WST** 2019 (~$75m revenue at acquisition), Aubin 2022.
- Lubricants: Detrex/Elco 2016, Polartech 2018.
- Also RecoPhos phosphorus-recovery technology and minority investments such as Eco Inhibitors.

In our universe, Compass (631) and BWA (12) are correctly rolled up. WST is missing and should be added, tagged mostly oilfield. We found no evidence of acquisitions named Aquapharm, Reunion or SCL; "Italmatch SC, LLC" is only a US legal entity.

### Competitive position
Italmatch is one of the global top-3 phosphonate producers, alongside Chinese producers and Zschimmer & Schwarz/Aquapharm. BWA brings a strong position in desalination antiscalants and specialty polymers. In US phosphonates it competes with Chinese imports, Kemira, SNF/Dow acrylics and Nouryon in chelants. Its moat is backward integration into phosphorus chlorides plus long-standing brands, though phosphonates are partly commoditised by Chinese capacity.

### Risks
- Chinese phosphonate price competition and anti-dumping dynamics.
- Oil & gas cyclicality in the US AWS business.
- Customer destocking, as seen in 2023.
- Leverage (~4x net debt/EBITDA) and change-of-control effects under a Dorf Ketal deal.
- Heavy reliance on a small number of global formulators.

### What is uncertain
The status of the Dorf Ketal transaction, FY2025 figures, the exact AWS split between water, oilfield and detergent, the US revenue share, and current headcount. All segment-level and US figures here are estimates derived as shown.
